recipes.name: Pasta e Fagioli
ingredients_raw: 2 cups Swanson® Chicken Broth or Swanson® Certified Organic Chicken Broth or Swanson® Natural Goodness® Chicken Broth
1 (15 ounce) can white kidney beans (cannellini), undrained
0.75 cup short tube-shaped ditalini pasta, cooked and drained

steps.text: Heat oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium heat. Cook and stir celery, carrots, onion, and garlic in hot oil until tender.
Stir broth, tomatoes, and Italian seasoning into vegetables in the skillet; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low and cook until vegetables are tender-crisp, about 15 minutes.
Add beans and pasta; cook until heated through, about 5 minutes.
Place 1/2 of the broth mixture into a blender or food processor. Cover and blend until smooth. Return puréed mixture to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, over medium heat until soup is hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Pasta e Fagioli
raw_recipe.description: This pasta e fagioli (pasta and beans) recipe is ready in only 45 minutes with lots of homemade flavor from fresh vegetables, pasta, and white kidney beans.

review.reviewBody: Super easy, super yummy. I too made adjustments based on what I had in my kitchen: Rotel canned tomatoes, no carrots (didn't realize I was out of them!!), Red kidney beans, a 14.5 oz can of chicken broth, shells instead of ditalini, and added green onions and shredded chicken. SO GOOD!! I love how adaptable this recipe is :)

Not bad at all. My Italian grandparents didn't put carrot or celery in it, I'm pretty sure that's either a 21st century thing or an American thing. They also didn't use "Italian Seasoning" because we put our seasonings in according to taste. Marjoram (in Italian Seasoning when you buy it all in one package) has no place in pasta e fagiole. At least one garlic clove needs to be smashed in at the end of the onion cooking so as not to burn it. I see people complain that this isn't like Olive Tree's but guess what? Olive Tree's pasta e fagiole is nothing like anything Italians make so.... Anyway the amounts this recipe calls for are well balanced, just use oregano and parsley as your Italian 'herbs' and even at that not too much Oregano. It's very perfumey if you use too much and will ruin the delicate taste of this wonderful rustic dish. No hot sauce please, no hot anything unless you're willing to name it something else because that's not pasta e fajiole. :) Oh, and no blending part of it. Sheesh. Just cook it and eat it. BTW it's delicious cold too.

Terrific. Changes. I added frozen corn, 8 oz of elbow mac (that's all I had), petite diced tomatoes with green chilis. I cooked the garlic separatly in olive oil and deglazed with the blender mixture. I pan fried in olive oil 2-3 chicken breasts coated with McCormick "Perfect Pinch" Vegetable Seasoning. Once the chicken was cooked I shreaded it and added it to the final mixture (I pan fried the shreaded chicken another couple of minutes before adding). I also added 1 tsp of the vegetable seasoning to the blender mixture when deglazing the garlic. I finished off the dish with 5 oz. of frozed chopped spinach. I went heavy on the vegetables and this made way more the 4 servings. I also ended up using about 4 cups of chicken broth. 5 stars by all who enjoyed.

LOVED this, though I did it a little differently. sauteed onions and lots of carrots, browned chicken pieces (after sprinkling with Italian seasoning), added white kidney beans and large can of tomatoes. I let this boil then added pasta and cooked a la dente. put into casserole dish with parm cheese on top and baked until cheese melted.
Easy and delicious. Sometimes we add one or two tempered eggs, spinach, and some parmasean cheese to make it a little heartier.

I gave this 5 stars only because this recipe is easy to customize based on what you already have. It's a flexible recipe that will be good even if you don't follow the exact measurements. I didn't have everything, so here is how I customized it. If you don't have Italian seasoning, you can instead use equal parts of basil, marjoram, oregano, rosemary and thyme. I didn't have rosemary but had all the others. I used 14.5 oz can chicken broth plus a little water since I didn't have 2 cups. I had a can of diced tomatoes with jalapeno's so I used that to make it nice and spicy! Finally, I used fresh cooked red kidney beans which is the reason I tried the recipe in the first place. A good recipe for using up left over veggies.
I’ve made this before following the directions. It was a little thicker then we like. So this time I skipped the blending step and it came out just the way we like it!

I would make it again. Since I am on weight watchers, I used whole wheat fusilli. In the time of covid, some substitutions are inevitable. I thought a couple of shakes of grated Parmesan greatly enhanced the flavor

I didn't have any problem with the way this tasted. I actually liked how hearty it was. The flavor was pretty good and even better with the shaved parmesan I put on top of my bowl. However, it took way longer than 45 minutes! To soften the vegetables it did take a good 15 minutes. I did keep the burner on medium, or setting 5 on my stove, so they did not burn. I did really like how many fresh vegetables were in it to. I used shell noodles and I microwaved them to save some time, which worked fine. With all the time spent though, I was kind of dissapointed in the only 3 average servings. I would definitely double it.
A keeper. Probably could’ve used more broth as a lot simmered off a more like a pasta dish vs a soup. Parmesan perfected it. Thanks! I might try with a good veg broth next time to make it vegetarian.

MADE THIS AND MY FAMILY LOVED IT. I ADDED EXTRA BROTH BECAUSE IT CAME OUT TOO THICK. EASY RECIPE TO FOLLOW AND COMES OUT VERY TASTY. THE MACARONI ABSORBS THE LIQUID SO I COOKED IT SEPERATELY BEFORE ADDING. THE GRANDKIDS LOVED IT SERVED WITH WARM ITALIAN BREAD
Super easy. Great taste. A true keeper. I added a piece of cheese rind for additional flavor.
So easy and absolutely delicious! This will become a staple at our house.
This is our favorite recipe and we add hot ground Italian sausage
Turned out great! I think I might add ground beef next time but it was great without it too.

This is a very easy soup to make and delicious. I made it exactly as the recipe was written but next time I will reduce the amount of Italian seasoning. It overwhelmed the other flavors. I might also add even more beans.
Update: Had the leftover soup today and it is even better the second day! I will definitely make it again.

Not even close to Olive Garden's Pasta E Fagoli. Lacks a lot of key ingredients: like seasoning, meat and sauce, making it EXTREMELY bland. Plus the directions were a little screwy near the end. I made it work.
Doubled the recipe. Could not make exactly son dislikes onions and celery. Delicious! Thank you

Made it as written but used red beans (all I had at the moment) instead of white. Loved it, but more importantly, my finicky husband loved it. Will plan on making double recipe from now on as someone suggested.
Pretty basic, but nice enough.
